headline: Japan Digital Nomad Visa 2026: Requirements, Limits and How to Apply
metaDescription: Japan digital nomad visa 2026: ¥10M income (~$63-70K), 6-month stay, launched March 2024. Income proof, insurance, family rules and application steps.

sections.content:
Japan's digital nomad visa, officially Designated Activities Status No. 53, launched in March 2024 as the country's first formal route for mid-term remote work. It allows eligible foreign nationals to live in Japan for up to six months while continuing to work remotely for overseas employers or clients.

The visa fixes the long-standing grey area of working while on a 90-day tourist stay, giving remote professionals a legal path to base themselves in Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto or Fukuoka for half a year. It targets high-earning remote workers and freelancers who can support themselves without entering Japan's labour market.
sections.title: What the Digital Nomad Visa Is

sections.content:
Applicants must demonstrate annual income of at least 10 million yen, roughly $63,000 to $70,000 depending on exchange rates, assessed on recent annual gross income. Accepted proof includes tax returns, employment certificates detailing salary, contracts and invoices; bank statements showing savings alone are not enough.

Nationality matters too: you must hold a passport from one of roughly 49 eligible countries that have visa-waiver agreements and tax treaties with Japan, including the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Singapore and EU member states. You also need private health insurance covering death, injury and illness for the entire stay, since Japan's National Health Insurance is not available to holders.
sections.title: Income, Nationality and Insurance Requirements

sections.content:
The six-month, non-renewable cap is the program's defining limitation. You cannot extend, renew or convert this visa, and no residence card is issued, which also means no Japanese bank account, no long-term phone contract and no standard apartment lease under typical terms.

Working for Japanese companies or invoicing Japanese clients is strictly prohibited; all income must come from foreign sources. Staying under 183 days in a calendar year generally keeps you outside Japanese tax residency, so foreign earnings remain taxed only in your home country, but day counts can accumulate across visits, so check with a tax professional.
sections.title: Limits: No Renewal, No Residence Card, No Local Work

sections.content:
Applications are filed at a Japanese embassy or consulate with your passport, proof of income, proof of private health insurance and documents showing your work is for entities outside Japan. Freelancers qualify as long as the income comes from clients or businesses based outside the country.

Spouses and children can accompany you under a related Designated Activities status, each with their own health insurance, but they may not work at all. If your partner also wants to work remotely, they must independently clear the 10-million-yen income bar and obtain their own visa.
